speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how old you are and if you have ever had a menstrual period? I would also like to know if you have broken any bones easily or have any unusual physical features you've noticed.

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of clitoromegaly, labial fusion, and maternal virilization during pregnancy, this strongly suggests congenital adrenal hyperplasia. REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone level

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That diagnosis of tuberculosis is incorrect and does not explain the virilization or bone fragility. I need to verify the hormonal imbalance and assess the bone health, so REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone level and DEXA scan.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: 17-hydroxyprogesterone: Elevated; DEXA scan: Osteoporosis (T-score -2.5 or lower)

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone confirms Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia, likely due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency, which explains both the virilization and the bone fragility from chronic cortisol deficiency. I need to check her adrenal androgen levels to assess the severity of the enzyme block. REQUEST TEST: Serum testosterone and androstenedione levels

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum testosterone: Elevated; Androstenedione: Elevated

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated androgens and 17-hydroxyprogesterone confirm non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia, which has led to osteoporosis and delayed menarche. DIAGNOSIS READY: Non-classic Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency)
